name: Amba (Uganda)
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible
sweep_summary: Amba (Uganda) is not in the catalog. The single works with stress in the title (Lucarini et al. 2021, psychiatry) is a Glottolog computerized mis-assignment from the title word 'disturbances' (record's language code field says so verbatim; saved) and is irrelevant. Cross-checking Glottolog 5.1 sources.bib held by the project: 32 refs tagged [rwm], 11 of them the same 'disturbances'/'initiates' keyword artifacts, the rest ethnography, wordlists (Struck 1910, de Wit-Hasselaar 1995) and overviews; no grammar or phonology exists in Glottolog for this language. The only descriptive source located is Tucker & Bryan 1957, Linguistic Survey of the Northern Bantu Borderland vol. 4, 'Characteristics of Amba (and Hyanz)' pp. 69-71 (Routledge DOI 10.4324/9781315105703-17), which is paywalled and HathiTrust search-only (v.4 mdp.39015070412872); priority medium for acquisition. No first-hand stress statement was read; no new stress statement was found. Saved files and at

Only the general transcription convention for all vocabularies (pp. 900-901): '' shows where the accent falls: in the absence of any mark the accent falls on the penultimate syllable.' Plus 'The Baamba attach e to the ends of nouns constantly.' Not a description of Kuamba stress.
